findings.text: Local datetime, date and time values carry a fixed zone with the local UTC offset. `v.In(time.UTC).Format(format)` shifts the wall clock by that offset before formatting. With offset +02:00, `2020-01-01T00:30:00` is encoded as `2019-12-31T22:30:00`, and `2020-01-01` becomes `2019-12-31`. Round-trips corrupt the value in any non-UTC timezone. The formatter should use `v` directly in its own location.

`parseTime` parses the local datetime, date or time string as UTC, then calls `t.In(l)` with the local-offset zone. `In` changes the wall clock by the offset, so `1987-07-05T17:45:00` becomes `19:45:00` at +02:00. The decoded expectation then disagrees with what the decoder produced. It should use `time.ParseInLocation` with `l`.
